title: Abu Dhabi launches global AI company to export 1,200 government services worldwide
source_used: The National (UAE); Arabian Business original blocked (HTTP 403)
key_facts: Abu Dhabi's Department of Government Enablement (DGE) announced on 16 Oct 2026 the creation of TAMM Global, under the directive of Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed, Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi and Chairman of the Abu Dhabi Executive Council.
TAMM Global will export the emirate's AI-powered unified government services platform, TAMM, to international markets.
It will develop, manage and deliver an integrated system of digital government services, owning and operating specialised digital platforms and holding the intellectual property rights.

As an independent private-sector company it will license the platform's architecture and implementation methods to governments, organisations and institutions worldwide, letting them adapt prebuilt services to their own laws.
TAMM brings together more than 1,200 public and private-sector services through one gateway, saving each user about nine visits to service centres a year, an estimated 12 hours.
Customer satisfaction rose to 94.5% from 78% in 2022, before AI was integrated, while the cost of providing services fell 30%.
Ahmed Al Kuttab, DGE chairman, said Abu Dhabi wants to make proven capabilities available to governments seeking better outcomes for their people.
quote_evidence: Abu Dhabi has established TAMM Global, a new company that will export the emirate's AI-powered unified government services platform to international markets.

As an independent private-sector company, TAMM Global will team up directly with governments, organisations and institutions worldwide, licensing the platform's architecture and implementation methodologies.

Customer satisfaction has risen to 94.5 per cent, up from 78 per cent in 2022, before artificial intelligence was integrated into the platform, while the cost of providing services has fallen by 30 per cent.
why_it_matters_hint: A Gulf government is turning its AI-run public-service platform into an export product for other governments.
notes: Arabian Business (pool source, HTTP 403) not opened; story read at The National, which reports the official DGE announcement. The performance figures are the Abu Dhabi government's own. The National says TAMM launched in 2005, which looks odd for the current platform, so the entry leaves that date out.
